title: Fix list health without missing BFCM
instructions: We need a sunset/re-permission program — deliverability says so — but I can't afford to shrink the mailable list right before our biggest quarter. Design the program and the timeline. Show me the tradeoff you're making.

parts.flow.json: {"flows": [...]} — the sunset/re-permission program as flow definitions (must reconcile the existing flow_sunset, not duplicate it)
parts.plan.md: program design, timeline vs. BFCM, and the quantified mailable-list/complaint-rate tradeoff

criteria.text: Submitted flow definitions are valid against the flow schema.

Sunset logic is consistent with the engagement data's actual tiers: the executed audience is drawn from real engagement_tier values and does not sweep in actively-engaged (engaged_30/engaged_90) profiles.

The proposed program interacts with the existing (currently disabled) flow_sunset by explicitly re-enabling or deprecating/replacing it — it does not sit untouched while a new flow duplicates its job.
Timeline sequences list hygiene correctly relative to BFCM: no full-file/full-list re-permission blast lands during the November BFCM ramp (goals/h2_targets.md: BFCM window Nov 20 – Dec 1).
Program complies with the deliverability report's stated house rules while elevated: no re-mailing of the deeper 24-month-inactive file, and full-list sends stay transactional-adjacent only.
The tradeoff quantification (mailable-list delta vs. complaint-rate projection) cites the environment's real numbers rather than invented figures.
Account invariants hold after the change and the 14-day ledger shows no harm events attributable to this work.
Sunset logic is engagement-tiered (differentiated treatment across engagement bands) rather than a single binary cutoff.
The program has explicit decision points with metrics (e.g., an engagement/response threshold that triggers suppression or wave progression) rather than a single unconditional pass.
Plan acknowledges the program's interaction with the frequency-fatigue problem (cadence increase driving complaints) rather than treating list hygiene in isolation.
